blocks.en: Software-Defined Networking
blocks.zh_html: 软件定义网络(software-defined networking, SDN)

blocks.en: Why Software-Defined Networking?
blocks.zh_html: 为什么需要软件定义网络(software-defined networking)？

blocks.en: Previously, we saw how routing protocols can be adapted to work in datacenter contexts (e.g. equal-cost multi-path). What if we want to optimize our routing protocols even further for our specific network’s constraints and use cases? The standard routing protocols might no longer work.
blocks.zh_html: 之前，我们看到了路由协议(routing protocols)如何被适配到数据中心环境(datacenter contexts)，例如等成本多路径(equal-cost multi-path)。如果我们想针对自己网络的特定约束和用例进一步优化路由协议呢？标准路由协议可能不再适用。

blocks.en: In this section, we’ll explore software-defined networking, a totally new paradigm for thinking about routing and network management. In the context of routing, the SDN architecture involves having a centralized control center compute routes and distribute them to individual routers. We’ll see how SDN works in the context of datacenters and the wide-area network, and discuss benefits and drawbacks of this new approach.
blocks.zh_html: 在本节中，我们将探索软件定义网络(software-defined networking, SDN)，这是一种思考路由(routing)和网络管理(network management)的完全新范式。在路由的背景下，SDN 架构涉及一个集中式控制中心(centralized control center)来计算路由并分发给各个路由器。我们将看到 SDN 如何工作在数据中心和广域网的背景下，并讨论这种新方法的优缺点。

blocks.en: Brief History of Software-Defined Networking
blocks.zh_html: 软件定义网络(software-defined networking)简史

blocks.en: Although we’ll be looking at SDN as a new approach for specialized routing protocols, the SDN paradigm was originally designed in response to headaches at the management plane.
blocks.zh_html: 虽然我们将把 SDN 看作一种用于专用路由协议的新方法，但 SDN 范式最初是为了响应管理平面(management plane)的痛点而设计的。

blocks.en: Recall that the management plane is critical for network operation. Routers can’t do anything unless someone configures them (e.g. assigns costs to links) and tells them what to do (e.g. what routing protocol to run). Also, we need routers to report errors to keep the network up and running. A lot of this management work has historically been done manually.
blocks.zh_html: 回想一下，管理平面(management plane)对网络运行至关重要。除非有人配置路由器(configures)，例如分配链路成本(costs)，并告诉它们该做什么，例如运行什么路由协议，否则路由器什么也做不了。此外，我们需要路由器报告错误，以保持网络的正常运行。历史上，这些管理工作很多是手动完成的。

blocks.en: Even though the management plane is so important, there’s been relatively little focus on innovating it. At the control plane, we’ve see lots of different routing protocols, but the way we configure and control routers has evolved more slowly.
blocks.zh_html: 尽管管理平面(management plane)如此重要，但对其创新的关注却相对较少。在控制平面(control plane)上，我们看到了许多不同的路由协议，但配置和控制路由器的方式演进得更慢。

blocks.en: Over the Internet’s history, there’s been a slow evolution toward using scripts to programatically interact with the network. These scripts take jobs that the operator would manually do, and implement them in code (without much intelligence). For example, scripts allow automating the process of adding routers and links to the network. A script for repairing the network might say: if a router fails, check that it’s actually failed, reboot it, and if it’s still not fixed, report to the operator.
blocks.zh_html: 在互联网的发展历程中，有一个缓慢的演进趋势：使用脚本(scripts)以编程方式与网络交互。这些脚本把操作员手动完成的任务用代码实现，但不需要太多智能。例如，脚本可以自动化添加路由器和链路到网络的过程。一个用于修复网络的脚本可能是：如果一台路由器发生故障，检查它是否真的故障了，重启它，如果仍然没有修复，则报告给操作员。

blocks.en: Despite the progress, these management systems have been the bottleneck for network operations for a long time. We still might have to wait for human intervention every time a new router is added.
blocks.zh_html: 尽管取得了进展，这些管理系统长期以来一直是网络运营的瓶颈。每次添加新路由器时，我们可能仍然需要等待人工干预。

blocks.en: In 2005, a paper by Albert Greenberg et. al. described the problem by saying: “Today’s data networks are surprisingly fragile and difficult to manage. We argue that the root of these problems lies in the complexity of the control and management planes.”
blocks.zh_html: 在 2005 年，Albert Greenberg 等人的一篇论文描述了这个问题："当今的数据网络出奇地脆弱且难以管理。我们认为这些问题的根源在于控制平面(control plane)和管理平面(management plane)的复杂性。"

blocks.en: In response to these problems, researchers began thinking about different ways to run a network system. This led to more radical proposals that reimagined the fundamental design of routers.
blocks.zh_html: 为了应对这些问题，研究人员开始思考运行网络系统的不同方式。这引出了更激进的方案，重新构想路由器的基本设计。

blocks.en: The concepts we’ll see were first considered in 2003, though they didn’t gain much momentum at the time. Frustrations with network management accelerated the development of new management paradigms. By 2008, there was more momentum, leading to the OpenFlow switch interface (which we’ll see soon).
blocks.zh_html: 我们将看到的概念最早在 2003 年被提出，尽管当时没有获得太多关注。对网络管理的不满加速了新管理范式的发展。到 2008 年，势头更强，催生了 OpenFlow 交换机接口(我们很快就会看到)。

blocks.en: By 2011, it was evident the industry was moving in this new direction, and the Open Networking Foundation (ONF) was established by major network operators (Google, Yahoo, Verizon, Microsoft, Facebook) and vendors (Cisco, Juniper, HP, Dell). Nicira, the SDN-focused startup that developed the OpenFlow interface, was a $40 million startup in 2012.
blocks.zh_html: 到 2011 年，行业显然正在朝着这个新方向发展，由主要网络运营商(Google、Yahoo、Verizon、Microsoft、Facebook)和设备商(Cisco、Juniper、HP、Dell)成立了开放网络基金会(ONF，Open Networking Foundation)。专注于 SDN 并开发了 OpenFlow 接口的初创公司 Nicira 在 2012 年估值 4000 万美元。

blocks.en: Routers are Vertically Integrated and Standardized
blocks.zh_html: 路由器是垂直集成(vertically integrated)且标准化(standardized)的

blocks.en: If we wanted to reimagine the design of routers, how would that be implemented in practice? How do technologies on routers change over time?
blocks.zh_html: 如果我们想重新构想路由器的设计，在实践中应如何实现？路由器上的技术如何随时间变化？

blocks.en: If your network needs a router, you’d probably purchase one from a major equipment vendor like Cisco or Juniper. In order to ensure that routers are compatible with each other, all the major equipment vendors build their routers according to some pre-defined standards.
blocks.zh_html: 如果你的网络需要一台路由器，你可能会从 Cisco 或 Juniper 等主要设备商那里购买。为了确保路由器彼此兼容，所有主要设备商都按照一些预定义的标准来构建他们的路由器。

blocks.en: This business model can make innovation and experimentation with new approaches difficult. Suppose you had a new idea for a routing protocol. You would need to get the protocol approved by a standards body, which could take years. Then, you’d have to wait for the vendors to upgrade their manufacturing to conform to the new standard.
blocks.zh_html: 这种商业模式可能使新方法的创新和实验变得困难。假设你有一个新的路由协议想法。你需要让标准组织批准该协议，这可能要花上几年。然后，你还需要等待设备商升级他们的制造工艺以符合新标准。

blocks.en: Standardization also makes routers less flexible for users implementing custom solutions. If you have a problem specific to your network, but no one else has this problem, your solution probably won’t be adopted by the standards body. Vendors want to make routers that satisfy everybody’s needs, and they won’t necessarily implement a solution that’s perfect for you, if nobody else wants it.
blocks.zh_html: 标准化(standardization)也使路由器对实施定制解决方案的用户来说不够灵活。如果你有一个针对自己网络的特定问题，但没有其他人有这个问题，你的解决方案很可能不会被标准组织采纳。设备商想制造能满足所有人需求的路由器，如果没有人想要，他们不一定会实现一个对你来说完美的解决方案。

blocks.en: On the other hand, standardization also means that if others have a problem that you don’t, the router might come with a solution to their problem, even if you don’t need it. This can make routers unnecessarily complex for the purposes of your specific network.
blocks.zh_html: 另一方面，标准化也意味着如果别人有你没有的问题，路由器可能会附带解决他们问题的方案，即使你并不需要。这可能会使路由器对你特定网络的需求来说不必要地复杂。

blocks.en: Standardization also makes experimentation and research difficult. If you want to try a new idea to see if it works, you might not be able to buy routers that can implement your new idea. Vendors don’t want to build experimental products, intended for one specific customer, that might not even work.
blocks.zh_html: 标准化也使实验和研究变得困难。如果你想尝试一个新想法看看是否有效，你可能买不到能实现你这个新想法的路由器。设备商不想制造实验性的产品，只为一个特定客户，而且还可能不成功。

blocks.en: Another major obstacle to innovation and experimentation is routers being vertically integrated. The router you buy already has the functionality for all three planes wired on the chips. There’s no modularity that would let you swap out just the control plane by itself.
blocks.zh_html: 创新和实验的另一个主要障碍是路由器是垂直集成(vertically integrated)的。你买的路由器三个平面的功能已经全部集成在芯片上。没有模块化(modularity)可以让你单独更换控制平面(control plane)。

blocks.en: Innovating Routers
blocks.zh_html: 路由器的创新

blocks.en: If we did want to innovate routers, what could we innovate at each plane, and what kinds of pre-existing standards would we be working with?
blocks.zh_html: 如果我们确实想对路由器进行创新，在每个平面我们可以创新什么？我们需要面对哪些现有标准？

blocks.en: The data plane is standardized by IEEE (electrical engineering group) and requires everyone to strictly follow the standards. If two routers from different vendors are connected, we have to make sure both sides are sending bits along the physical wire in the same consistent format.
blocks.zh_html: 数据平面(data plane)由 IEEE(电子工程组织)标准化，要求每个人都严格遵守标准。如果来自不同设备商的两台路由器相连，我们必须确保双方以相同一致的格式沿着物理线路发送比特。

blocks.en: Data plane innovation is usually driven by the demand for higher-bandwidth routers, and new features are not often introduced. This development happens quite slowly, in 2-3 year increments, because we have to solve physical hardware problems and design chips for increased bandwidth. Since the core data plane features are relatively stable, router innovation is not really focused on the data plane, and it’s okay that the development cycle is slow.
blocks.zh_html: 数据平面(data plane)的创新通常由对更高带宽路由器的需求驱动，新功能不常引入。这种发展相当缓慢，以 2 到 3 年为周期，因为我们必须解决物理硬件问题并设计芯片以提高带宽。由于核心数据平面功能相对稳定，路由器的创新并不真正集中在数据平面上，并且开发周期慢也是可以接受的。

blocks.en: The control plane is standardized by the IETF (the network group behind RFCs). Vendors sometimes add their own extensions, though the core features are mostly standardized. For example, we assume that every router (even if they’re from different routers) are following the same routing protocol.
blocks.zh_html: 控制平面(control plane)由 IETF(负责 RFC 的网络组织)标准化。设备商有时会添加自己的扩展，但核心功能大多是标准化的。例如，我们假设每台路由器，即使来自不同设备商，都遵循相同的路由协议。

blocks.en: Control plane innovation (e.g. new routing protocols) can take several years to be adopted. You might have to submit an RFC draft proposal, and the community may spend some time discussing the proposal before agreeing on its terms.
blocks.zh_html: 控制平面(control plane)的创新(例如新的路由协议)可能需要数年才能被采纳。你可能需要提交一份 RFC 草案，社区需要花一些时间讨论该提案，然后才能就条款达成一致。

blocks.en: The management plane is also standardized by the IETF, though it’s much less standardized. Different operators can use different software to configure their routers, and we don’t really need different vendors to agree on some standardized software. Because this plane is only loosely standardized, many different approaches with different features exist.
blocks.zh_html: 管理平面(management plane)也由 IETF 标准化，但标准化程度低得多。不同运营方可以使用不同软件来配置他们的路由器，我们并不真的需要不同设备商就某种标准化软件达成一致。由于这个平面只是松散地标准化，存在许多具有不同功能的方法。

blocks.en: In summary: The data plane is standardized (but we don’t really have new features in mind), the control plane is standardized (but we want to try new solutions), and the management plane is not really standardized.
blocks.zh_html: 总结一下：数据平面(data plane)是标准化的(但我们并没有真正想要的新功能)，控制平面(control plane)是标准化的(但我们想尝试新方案)，而管理平面(management plane)并没有真正标准化。

blocks.en: Radical Idea: Disaggregating Routers
blocks.zh_html: 激进想法：解耦路由器(disaggregating routers)

blocks.en: Standardization and vertical integration were making it difficult to innovate and experiment. This led to the radical idea of disaggregating routers by splitting the planes into different layers of abstraction. Instead of buying a single router with all three planes, we could now buy data and control plane functionality separately. This allows us to change layers independently from each other.
blocks.zh_html: 标准化(standardization)和垂直集成(vertical integration)使创新和实验变得困难。这引出了解耦路由器(disaggregating routers)的激进想法：把平面拆分为不同的抽象层(abstraction layers)。与其购买一台包含所有三个平面的路由器，我们可以分别购买数据平面和控制平面功能。这允许我们独立地更改各层。

blocks.en: In order to connect the three layers, we need an API between the layers of abstraction. In a vertically-coupled router, we don’t care how the data plane and control plane talk to each other. However, if we buy the data plane separately, and we want to design our own custom control plane on top, we need an interface to interact with the data plane.
blocks.zh_html: 为了连接这三层，我们需要在抽象层(abstraction layers)之间有一个 API。在垂直耦合(vertically-coupled)的路由器中，我们不关心数据平面(data plane)和控制平面(control plane)如何交互。但是，如果我们分开购买数据平面，并想在上面设计自己的自定义控制平面，就需要一个接口来与数据平面交互。

blocks.en: An even more radical idea is to stop thinking about the three planes in terms of only the router, and instead design a new system architecture that naturally splits up the data plane and control plane.
blocks.zh_html: 一个更激进的想法是，不再仅仅从路由器的角度思考这三个平面，而是设计一种新的系统架构，自然地分离数据平面(data plane)和控制平面(control plane)。

blocks.en: At the bottom, we have commodity network devices. You can think of these as buying just the data plane by itself. These routers receive instructions from the control program via the network OS, and simply forward packets according to those instructions. These routers don’t need to think about routing protocols at all, so they can be cheaper.
blocks.zh_html: 在底层，我们有通用网络设备(commodity network devices)。你可以把这看作只购买数据平面(data plane)本身。这些路由器通过网络 OS 从控制程序接收指令，并根据这些指令简单地转发分组(forward packets)。这些路由器完全不需要考虑路由协议，因此可以更便宜。

blocks.en: In the middle, we have the network OS. You can think of this as the API connecting the data plane routers and the control plane program. The network OS provides an abstraction of the routers (e.g. as a graph) that can be passed up to the control program. Then, the control program can send routing instructions to the network OS, without worrying about how to program specific routers. The network OS can take those instructions and program them onto individual routers.
blocks.zh_html: 在中间层，我们有网络 OS(network OS)。你可以把这看作连接数据平面路由器(控制平面程序)的 API。网络 OS 提供路由器的抽象(abstraction)，例如以图(graph)的形式，可以向上传递给控制程序。然后，控制程序可以向网络 OS 发送路由指令，而无需担心如何编程特定路由器。网络 OS 可以接收这些指令并将它们编程到各个路由器上。

blocks.en: At the top, we have the control program. You can think of this as buying or implementing the control plane by itself. Here, the operator receives an abstraction of the network (e.g. graph) from the network OS, and can use that to write their own custom routing protocol. Then, the resulting routes can be passed to the network OS, which will program them onto routers.
blocks.zh_html: 在最上层，我们有控制程序(control program)。你可以把这看作单独购买或实现控制平面(control plane)。在这里，操作员从网络 OS 接收网络的抽象(如图)，并可以用它来编写自己的自定义路由协议。然后，生成的路由可以传递给网络 OS，网络 OS 再将它们编程到路由器上。

blocks.en: OpenFlow API Format
blocks.zh_html: OpenFlow API 格式

blocks.en: OpenFlow is an API for interacting with the data plane of a router. The operator writes their own fancy code, separate from the router, that computes routes through the network. Then, those routes can be programmed onto the forwarding chip.
blocks.zh_html: OpenFlow 是一个用于与路由器数据平面(data plane)交互的 API。操作员编写自己的高级代码，独立于路由器，计算通过网络的路径。然后，这些路径可以被编程到转发芯片(forwarding chip)上。

blocks.en: The OpenFlow paradigm is different from traditional routers, where the control plane is implemented in the router, and there’s no clear API for programming custom routes onto the forwarding chip.
blocks.zh_html: OpenFlow 范式不同于传统路由器，后者控制平面(control plane)在路由器内部实现，没有清晰的 API 用于在转发芯片上编程自定义路由。

blocks.en: The OpenFlow API defines a flow table abstraction to describe routes and forwarding rules. The operator code can output any rules and routes it wants, and install them on the router, as long as they’re in the flow table format.
blocks.zh_html: OpenFlow API 定义了一个流表(flow table)抽象(abstraction)来描述路由和转发规则。操作员代码可以输出任何想要的规则和路由，并将它们安装到路由器上，只要它们符合流表格式。

blocks.en: The basic building block of the API is a flow table, which you can think of as a generalized version of a forwarding table. Each flow table consists of key-value pairs, just like a forwarding table. The key specifies what to match the packet against. This could be a destination prefix, an exact destination, a 5-tuple, or other relatively simple matches. The corresponding value specifies what action to set when a packet matches. The action could be sending the packet to a next hop (like a forwarding table), but could also specify fancier actions like adding an extra header.
blocks.zh_html: API 的基本构建模块是流表(flow table)，你可以把它看作是转发表(forwarding table)的通用版本。每个流表由键值对(key-value pairs)组成，就像转发表一样。键指定要对分组进行什么匹配(match)。这可以是目的前缀(destination prefix)、确切目的地(exact destination)、五元组(5-tuple)或其他相对简单的匹配。对应的值指定当分组匹配时要执行什么动作(action)。动作可以是把分组发送到下一跳(next hop)，就像转发表那样，但也可以指定更复杂的动作，比如添加额外首部(extra header)。

blocks.en: The output format is a sequence of one or more numbered flow tables, where each table has its own different match-action entries. These flow tables can then be programmed onto the forwarding chip.
blocks.zh_html: 输出格式是一个由一个或多个编号流表组成的序列，每个表有自己的不同匹配-动作条目。这些流表然后可以被编程到转发芯片(forwarding chip)上。

blocks.en: When a packet arrives at a router, it is checked against each table in order (e.g. Table 0, Table 1, Table 2, etc.), and when there’s a match, we write down the corresponding action (without executing it yet). Eventually, once the packet is checked against the final table, any action(s) we wrote down are applied to the packet.
blocks.zh_html: 当一个分组(packet)到达路由器时，会按顺序与每个表进行比对，例如表 0、表 1、表 2 等。当匹配时，我们记录下相应的动作，但先不执行。最终，在分组与最后一个表比对完毕后，之前记录的任何动作都会应用到该分组上。

blocks.en: There are also special actions for skipping to later tables, which we can use in rules like: If the source port matches this number, skip to table 5 to set additional actions.
blocks.zh_html: 还有一些特殊动作可以跳过到后面的表，我们可以用在这样的规则中：如果源端口匹配这个数字，跳到表 5 来设置额外的动作。

blocks.en: The operator can run any code they want to generate flow tables, and the flow tables can be more general than a destination/next-hop forwarding table. However, the rules (match/action pairs) that we generate are still constrained by the specialized forwarding chip hardware. The forwarding chip is optimized for speed, and probably can’t handle complex match rules like “if the TCP payload is in English, set this action.”
blocks.zh_html: 操作员可以运行任何他们想要的代码来生成流表，而流表可以比目的/下一跳转发表更通用。然而，我们生成的规则(匹配/动作对)仍然受限于专门的转发芯片硬件。转发芯片针对速度进行了优化，很可能无法处理像"如果 TCP 负载是英文，设置这个动作"这样的复杂匹配规则。

blocks.en: As a result, the flow tables we see in practice end up looking pretty similar to the tables we’ve already seen. Common match rules include longest prefix matching on IP destinations, 5-tuples to identify flows, and exact matches on encapsulation headers (e.g. MPLS).
blocks.zh_html: 因此，我们在实践中看到的流表最终看起来与我们已经见过的表非常相似。常见的匹配规则包括 IP 目的地的 最长前缀匹配(longest prefix matching)、用于标识流的五元组(5-tuples)，以及封装首部(encapsulation headers)的精确匹配(例如 MPLS)。

blocks.en: If the forwarding rules aren’t so different, why use OpenFlow at all? Remember, the main advantage is that it gives the operator total freedom at the control plane. We’re not limited to distance-vector or link-state protocols anymore.
blocks.zh_html: 如果转发规则没有太大区别，那为什么还要使用 OpenFlow 呢？记住，主要优势是它给了操作员在控制平面(control plane)上的完全自由。我们不再局限于距离向量(distance-vector)或链路状态(link-state)协议。

blocks.en: Benefits of a Flexible Control Plane
blocks.zh_html: 灵活控制平面(flexible control plane)的好处

blocks.en: Our new architecture gives the operator flexibility to implement their new routing protocol at the control plane. What are some benefits of this approach?
blocks.zh_html: 我们的新架构让操作员可以在控制平面(control plane)上灵活地实现他们自己的路由协议。这种方法有什么好处？

blocks.en: The operator can implement custom routing protocols best-suited for the operator’s specific needs. The operator is no longer constrained by standards bodies and vendors.
blocks.zh_html: 操作员可以实现最适合自己特定需求的自定义路由协议(custom routing protocols)。操作员不再受标准组织和设备商的约束。

blocks.en: Flexibility also gives us an opportunity to simplify. For example, if the standardized protocol includes features we don’t need, we don’t have to implement them in our custom solution. Simpler protocols can have less code and simpler code, which might allow for easier development and maintenance of that protocol.
blocks.zh_html: 灵活性也给了我们简化的机会。例如，如果标准化协议包含我们不需要的功能，我们就不必在自定义方案中实现它们。更简单的协议可以有更少的代码和更简单的代码，这可能使该协议的开发和维护更容易。

blocks.en: Finally, a flexible control plane enables centralized computation of routes at the control program, instead of distributed across multiple routers. Centralization comes with several benefits as well.
blocks.zh_html: 最后，灵活的控制平面(control plane)可以在控制程序(control program)处实现集中式路由计算，而不是分布在多个路由器上。集中化(centralization)也带来了几个好处。

blocks.en: Centralization can result in more intelligent routing decisions that lead to excellent performance. In a 2013 report from Google, engineers who deployed an SDN architecture noted that “centralized traffic engineering service drives links to near 100% utilization, while splitting application flows among multiple paths to balance capacity against application priority/demands.” A 2013 paper from Microsoft describes using an OpenFlow controller to “achieve high utilization with software-driven WAN.”
blocks.zh_html: 集中化(centralization)可以带来更智能的路由决策，实现卓越的性能。在 Google 工程师的一份 2013 年报告中，部署了 SDN 架构的工程师指出："集中式流量工程服务将链路利用率驱动到接近 100%，同时将应用流(application flows)分配到多条路径上，以平衡容量与应用优先级/需求。"Microsoft 在 2013 年的一篇论文中描述了使用 OpenFlow 控制器"通过软件驱动的 WAN 实现高利用率"。

blocks.en: More intelligent routing decisions can help optimize other criteria besides performance, that a standard routing protocol can’t easily optimize. For example, a US government network might implement a geofencing rule that says, don’t send traffic via links that are in Canada. Or, a broadcast TV network might want to optimize for path diversity to increase reliability. We can enforce that two flows travel via paths that don’t share any links, so that if a link goes down, only one of the flows is affected. The two paths can serve as backups for each other.
blocks.zh_html: 更智能的路由决策可以帮助优化除了性能之外的其他指标，而标准路由协议不容易优化这些指标。例如，美国政府网络可能实现一个地理围栏(geofencing)规则：不通过位于加拿大的链路发送流量。或者，广播电视网络可能想要优化路径多样性(path diversity)以提高可靠性。我们可以强制两个流经由不共享任何链路的路径传输，这样如果一条链路中断，只有一个流受到影响。这两条路径可以互为备份。

blocks.en: Centralization can also make it easier for routing protocols to converge. In a distributed protocol, if the network changed, the routers have to coordinate to converge on a new routing state. In this centralized model, if a link fails, that router could tell the boss, and the boss could recompute routes and install the new routes on the routers.
blocks.zh_html: 集中化(centralization)还可以使路由协议更容易收敛(converge)。在分布式协议中，如果网络发生变化，路由器必须协调以收敛到新的路由状态。在这种集中式模型中，如果一条链路发生故障，该路由器可以告诉"老板"，老板可以重新计算路由并在路由器上安装新路由。

blocks.en: Traffic Engineering
blocks.zh_html: 流量工程(traffic engineering)

blocks.en: A flexible control plane allows us to perform traffic engineering, which means we can route traffic in a more intelligent and efficient way than a standard distributed routing protocol could.
blocks.zh_html: 灵活的控制平面(control plane)允许我们执行流量工程(traffic engineering)，这意味着我们可以以比标准分布式路由协议更智能、更高效的方式路由流量。

blocks.en: Suppose there are two connections, S1-D at 10 Gbps and S2-D at 10 Gbps. If we just ran standard least-cost routing, both flows would send traffic along the bottom path. The bottom path would be congested (20 Gbps on 10 Gbps link), while the top path’s bandwidth is sitting there unused.
blocks.zh_html: 假设有两个连接，S1-D 为 10 Gbps，S2-D 为 10 Gbps。如果我们只运行标准的最少成本路由(least-cost routing)，两个流都会沿着底部路径发送流量。底部路径会拥塞(congested)，10 Gbps 链路上有 20 Gbps，而顶部路径的带宽则闲置不用。

blocks.en: With a more intelligent routing scheme, we could send S1-D traffic along the top path, and S2-D traffic along the bottom path. Using traffic engineering, we’ve forced some packets to take a longer route, in order to better utilize the bandwidth in the network.
blocks.zh_html: 通过更智能的路由方案，我们可以把 S1-D 的流量沿顶部路径发送，S2-D 的流量沿底部路径发送。通过流量工程(traffic engineering)，我们强制一些分组走更长的路径，以更好地利用网络中的带宽。

blocks.en: To compute these routes, we can modify least-cost routing, and instead enforce that traffic should be on the shortest path that has sufficient capacity. We can also enforce other constraints instead of capacity, such as latency. The resulting algorithm is called constrained Shortest Path First (cSPF).
blocks.zh_html: 为了计算这些路由，我们可以修改最少成本路由(least-cost routing)，改为强制要求流量应该走有足够容量的最短路径。我们还可以施加其他约束，比如延迟(latency)，而不是容量。由此产生的算法称为约束最短路径优先(cSPF，constrained Shortest Path First)。

blocks.en: Now, suppose that S1-D needs 12 Gbps, and S2-D needs 8 Gbps. cSPF will send the flows along different paths to maximize bandwidth, but S1-D is sending 12 Gbps over a 10 Gbps link.
blocks.zh_html: 现在，假设 S1-D 需要 12 Gbps，S2-D 需要 8 Gbps。cSPF 会沿不同路径发送这些流以最大化带宽，但 S1-D 在 10 Gbps 链路上发送 12 Gbps。

blocks.en: To fix this, our traffic engineering can be even more intelligent, and split traffic in a flow across different paths. S1-D can send 10 Gbps of its traffic along the top path, and the remaining 2 Gbps along the bottom path.
blocks.zh_html: 为了解决这个问题，我们的流量工程(traffic engineering)可以更加智能，把一个流中的流量分摊到不同路径上。S1-D 可以沿顶部路径发送 10 Gbps 的流量，剩余 2 Gbps 沿底部路径发送。

blocks.en: Again, our traffic engineering allowed us to implement custom logic that resulted in better utilization of the network capacity.
blocks.zh_html: 再次，我们的流量工程(traffic engineering)允许我们实现自定义逻辑，从而更好地利用网络容量。

blocks.en: How do we actually implement split paths through the network, using the OpenFlow API from earlier? Remember, our routing decisions should still follow simple rules that forwarding tables can understand.
blocks.zh_html: 我们如何实际利用前面的 OpenFlow API 来实现网络中的拆分路径(split paths)？记住，我们的路由决策仍然应该遵循转发表(forwarding tables)能理解的简单规则。

blocks.en: One approach is to use encapsulation. At the sender, we can add rules to add an extra header, where some packets get label 0, and the rest get label 1. This label tells us which path to send the traffic along.
blocks.zh_html: 一种方法是使用封装(encapsulation)。在发送端，我们可以添加规则来增加一个额外首部(extra header)，其中一些分组获得标签 0，其余获得标签 1。这个标签告诉我们应该沿哪条路径发送流量。

blocks.en: Now, at R1, we can add simple rules to route label 0 packets upwards to R2, and label 1 packets downwards to R3. This idea can be applied in addition to the other rules we had for constrained least-cost routing (e.g. the flow tables might have other entries for other destinations or other flows).
blocks.zh_html: 现在，在 R1 上，我们可以添加简单规则：标签 0 的分组向上路由到 R2，标签 1 的分组向下路由到 R3。这个想法可以与我们已有的约束最少成本路由(constrained least-cost routing)的其他规则一起应用，例如流表中可能还有其他目的地或其他流的条目。

blocks.en: Centralized Traffic Engineering and Globally Optimal Decisions
blocks.zh_html: 集中式流量工程(centralized traffic engineering)与全局最优决策(globally optimal decisions)

blocks.en: One major difference in the SDN model of custom routing protocols is centralization. In the original model, every router was running its own routing protocol. Now, we can have a single computer outside of the routers compute all the routes, and then use the flow table API to install those routes on the routers.
blocks.zh_html: SDN 自定义路由协议模型的一个主要区别是集中化(centralization)。在原始模型中，每台路由器都运行自己的路由协议。现在，我们可以有一台独立于路由器的计算机来计算所有路由，然后使用流表 API 将这些路由安装到路由器上。

blocks.en: Centralization allows us to make globally optimal decisions. In a distributed protocol, each router is making the best decision for itself, but that might not be the best decision for other routers. In the centralized model, the boss can use its global view of the network to decide what’s best for everybody, and tell the routers to follow that decision.
blocks.zh_html: 集中化(centralization)允许我们做出全局最优决策(globally optimal decisions)。在分布式协议中，每台路由器都在为自己做出最佳决策，但这可能不是对其他路由器的最佳决策。在集中式模型中，"老板"可以利用其全局网络视图来决定对所有人来说什么是最优的，并告诉路由器遵循该决策。

blocks.en: Consider this network with two flows, S1-D at 20 Gbps, and S2-D at 100 Gbps. Assume we haven’t implemented support for splitting a flow onto multiple paths.
blocks.zh_html: 考虑这个有两个流的网络：S1-D 为 20 Gbps，S2-D 为 100 Gbps。假设我们还没有实现把流拆分到多条路径的支持。

blocks.en: Suppose the 20 Gbps S1-D flow starts first. Using constrained shortest path first, S1 could choose to use the bottom path. From the perspective of S1, this is a locally optimal decision (top and bottom paths both equally good).
blocks.zh_html: 假设 20 Gbps 的 S1-D 流先开始。使用约束最短路径优先(constrained shortest path first)，S1 可以选择使用底部路径。从 S1 的角度来看，这是一个局部最优决策(顶部和底部路径同样好)。

blocks.en: Later, the 100 Gbps S2-D flow starts. Now, using constrained shortest path first, S2-D doesn’t have any single path that meets its demands. The top path (20 Gbps) and bottom path (80 Gbps) both have insufficient capacity.
blocks.zh_html: 后来，100 Gbps 的 S2-D 流开始。现在使用约束最短路径优先，S2-D 没有一条能单独满足其需求的路径。顶部路径(20 Gbps)和底部路径(80 Gbps)的容量都不够。

blocks.en: The key problem here is, each individual router made its own decision independently, without coordination.
blocks.zh_html: 这里的关键问题是：每台路由器独立做出自己的决策，没有相互协调。

blocks.en: By introducing a centralized controller, the controller can look at the overall network structure and the demands of each flow, and assign paths to each flow more intelligently. The resulting decision is globally optimal, and increases network efficiency.
blocks.zh_html: 通过引入集中式控制器(centralized controller)，控制器可以查看整体网络结构和每个流的需求，更智能地为每个流分配路径。由此产生的决策是全局最优的，提高了网络效率。

blocks.en: Centralized traffic engineering can make even more intelligent routing decisions, depending on what the operator wants to optimize. For example, we could classify flows as high-priority or low-priority, and make decisions that optimize both network utilization and the needs of different applications.
blocks.zh_html: 集中式流量工程(centralized traffic engineering)可以根据操作员想要优化的目标做出更智能的路由决策。例如，我们可以把流分类为高优先级或低优先级，并做出同时优化网络利用率和不同应用需求的决策。

blocks.en: SDN in Datacenter Overlay
blocks.zh_html: 数据中心覆盖网络(datacenter overlay)中的 SDN

blocks.en: In the previous section, we saw that virtual switches can apply encapsulation to connect the overlay and underlay networks. Given a virtual address, we can add a header with the corresponding physical address, which allows the packet to be sent along the underlay network. But, how do we know the mapping between virtual addresses and physical addresses?
blocks.zh_html: 在上一节中，我们看到虚拟交换机(virtual switches)可以应用封装(encapsulation)来连接覆盖网络(overlay)和底层网络(underlay)。给定一个虚拟地址(virtual address)，我们可以添加一个包含对应物理地址的首部(header)，使分组可以沿底层网络发送。但是，我们如何知道虚拟地址和物理地址之间的映射？

blocks.en: We also saw that encapsulation can be used to to support multiple tenants in a single datacenter, each running their own private network. Switches can add headers with a virtual network ID. But, how do we know which virtual network ID to use?
blocks.zh_html: 我们还看到封装(encapsulation)可用于支持单个数据中心中的多个租户(multiple tenants)，每个租户运行自己的私有网络(private network)。交换机(switches)可以添加带有虚拟网络 ID(virtual network ID)的首部。但是，我们如何知道使用哪个虚拟网络 ID？

blocks.en: A centralized SDN controller can be used in the datacenter to solve these problems. Each tenant can operate its own controller. When a new VM is created, the SDN learns about its virtual and physical addresses. Then, the SDN can update the forwarding tables in the other virtual switches, adding encapsulation rules with the new virtual/physical address mapping.
blocks.zh_html: 集中式 SDN 控制器(centralized SDN controller)可以在数据中心中用来解决这些问题。每个租户可以运行自己的控制器。当创建新的 VM 时，SDN 会了解其虚拟地址和物理地址。然后，SDN 可以更新其他虚拟交换机中的转发表，添加带有新虚拟/物理地址映射的封装规则。

blocks.en: For example, suppose Coke VM 2 is created with virtual IP 192.0.2.1 and physical IP 2.2.2.2. The SDN knows Coke VM 1 lives on physical server 1.1.1.1, so it can go to the virtual switch on 1.1.1.1 and add an encapsulation rule for the new Coke VM 2.
blocks.zh_html: 例如，假设 Coke VM 2 被创建，虚拟 IP 为 192.0.2.1，物理 IP 为 2.2.2.2。SDN 知道 Coke VM 1 在物理服务器 1.1.1.1 上，因此它可以去 1.1.1.1 上的虚拟交换机，为新的 Coke VM 2 添加封装规则。

blocks.en: The flow table at 1.1.1.1 might say: If you receive a packet with destination 192.0.2.1, add a header with Coke’s virtual network ID of 42. Also, add a header with the corresponding physical address 2.2.2.2. Then, send the packet along the underlay network.
blocks.zh_html: 1.1.1.1 上的流表可能是：如果你收到一个目的地址为 192.0.2.1 的分组，添加一个带有 Coke 的虚拟网络 ID 42 的首部。同时，添加一个带有对应物理地址 2.2.2.2 的首部。然后，沿底层网络发送该分组。

blocks.en: Benefits of SDN in Datacenter Overlay
blocks.zh_html: 数据中心覆盖网络(datacenter overlay)中 SDN 的好处

blocks.en: Why might we use a centralized SDN architecture to support virtualization and multi-tenancy in datacenters, instead of a more standard routing protocol?
blocks.zh_html: 为什么我们要使用集中式 SDN 架构来支持数据中心中的虚拟化(virtualization)和多租户(multi-tenancy)，而不是使用更标准的路由协议？

blocks.en: The centralized SDN architecture allows us to cleanly split the overlay and underlay networks into two scalable layers. In a traditional architecture, the routers in the underlay network would have to process the custom encapsulation headers (e.g. virtual network IDs). SDN allows the underlay network to remain simple, without thinking about virtualization or multi-tenancy.
blocks.zh_html: 集中式 SDN 架构允许我们把覆盖网络(overlay)和底层网络(underlay)干净地拆分为两个可扩展的层。在传统架构中，底层网络中的路由器必须处理自定义封装首部(如虚拟网络 ID)。SDN 允许底层网络保持简单，不需要考虑虚拟化(virtualization)或多租户(multi-tenancy)。

blocks.en: Centralization gives us a simple way to implement the control plane at end hosts, without any complicated routing protocols. The controller learns about a new host and updates the other hosts accordingly. Without a centralized controller, we might need some complex distributed scheme to figure out which encapsulation headers to add.
blocks.zh_html: 集中化(centralization)为我们提供了一种在端主机(end hosts)上实现控制平面(control plane)的简单方法，无需复杂路由协议。控制器了解新主机，并相应地更新其他主机。如果没有集中式控制器，我们可能需要某种复杂的分布式方案来确定要添加哪些封装首部。

blocks.en: This SDN architecture also shows us why overlay networks can scale well. The SDN controller for a tenant only needs to know about the VMs belonging to that specific tenant. By contrast, if we used a traditional architecture, a new Coke VM might have to be advertised to all the other VMs, even Pepsi VMs.
blocks.zh_html: 这种 SDN 架构也展示了覆盖网络(overlay networks)为什么可以很好地扩展。租户的 SDN 控制器只需要知道属于该特定租户的 VM。相比之下，如果我们使用传统架构，一个新的 Coke VM 可能不得不向所有其他 VM 广播，甚至包括 Pepsi 的 VM。

blocks.en: SDN in Datacenter Underlay
blocks.zh_html: 数据中心底层网络(datacenter underlay)中的 SDN

blocks.en: The datacenter underlay is a physical network, just like any other network, although with a special topology. Many general-purpose network challenges, like achieving high utilization of links, also apply to datacenter underlay networks. That means we can apply SDN to the underlay network as well.
blocks.zh_html: 数据中心底层网络(datacenter underlay)是一个物理网络(physical network)，就像任何其他网络一样，尽管具有特殊的拓扑结构。许多通用网络挑战，比如实现链路的高利用率，也适用于数据中心底层网络。这意味着我们也可以将 SDN 应用于底层网络。

blocks.en: SDN at the underlay network can help us efficiently route packets through the datacenter. For example, the operator might want to send mice flows along links with small delay, and elephant flows along links with high bandwidth.
blocks.zh_html: 底层网络(underlay network)上的 SDN 可以帮助我们高效地通过数据中心路由分组(packets)。例如，操作员可能希望把小鼠流(mice flows)沿延迟小的链路发送，把大象流(elephant flows)沿带宽高的链路发送。

blocks.en: In our underlay Clos network, per-flow load balancing (hash 5-tuple to choose a path) could still send multiple elephant flows along the same path. Even if two elephant flows used different paths, the paths might share links, and those links might become congested. An SDN controller could solve this problem by coordinating the flows and placing them onto non-overlapping paths.
blocks.zh_html: 在我们底层 Clos 网络中，每流负载均衡(per-flow load balancing，对五元组哈希以选择路径)仍可能把多个大象流发送到同一条路径。即使两个大象流使用了不同路径，这些路径也可能共享链路，而这些链路可能会变得拥塞。SDN 控制器可以通过协调这些流并将它们放置到不重叠的路径上来解决这个问题。

blocks.en: This 2022 Google paper describes eliminating layers in the Clos network (fewer links, cheaper datacenter) by using SDN to route traffic more intelligently.
blocks.zh_html: 这篇 2022 年的 Google 论文描述了通过使用 SDN 更智能地路由流量，来消除 Clos 网络中的层(更少的链路、更便宜的数据中心)。

blocks.en: Hyperscale datacenters often use SDN in both the overlay and underlay networks. These are usually implemented as decoupled systems. There’s one SDN thinking about the underlay, and a separate SDN thinking about the overlay.
blocks.zh_html: 超大规模数据中心(hyperscale datacenters)通常在覆盖网络(overlay)和底层网络(underlay)中都使用 SDN。这些通常作为解耦的系统实现。有一个 SDN 考虑底层网络，另一个独立的 SDN 考虑覆盖网络。

blocks.en: SDN in Wide Area Networks
blocks.zh_html: 广域网(WAN)中的 SDN

blocks.en: In addition to datacenters, SDN can be useful in general wide-area networks, especially when efficient utilization of bandwidth is critical. For example, in the traffic engineering example from earlier, imagine if our 10 Gbps links were undersea cables. There’s no cheap way to add additional bandwidth, so optimizations have to instead focus on efficient utilization of the bandwidth we do have.
blocks.zh_html: 除了数据中心，SDN 在通用广域网(wide-area networks)中也很有用，特别是当带宽的高效利用至关重要时。例如，在之前的流量工程例子中，想象一下，如果我们的 10 Gbps 链路是海底电缆。没有廉价的方法来增加额外带宽，因此优化必须集中在高效利用我们已有的带宽上。

blocks.en: Drawbacks of Centralized Control
blocks.zh_html: 集中式控制(centralized control)的缺点

blocks.en: Centralization doesn’t come for free, and has some drawbacks.
blocks.zh_html: 集中化(centralization)并非没有代价，它有一些缺点。

blocks.en: One drawback is reliability. In a traditional network, if a router fails, the routing protocol converges around the failure. The other routers can reroute traffic along other paths. By contrast, if the central controller fails, we don’t have a way to update the network anymore, and the routers don’t know how to adjust to changes.
blocks.zh_html: 一个缺点是可靠性(reliability)。在传统网络中，如果一台路由器发生故障，路由协议会围绕故障收敛(converge)。其他路由器可以沿其他路径重新路由流量。相反，如果中央控制器发生故障，我们就没有办法再更新网络了，路由器不知道如何适应变化。

blocks.en: Note: We’ve drawn the centralized controller as a single entity, but it doesn’t need to be run on a single server. The control plane computation could happen across multiple servers, where those servers coordinate to operate in a logically centralized way. This is different from the original model, where routers coordinated but still made their own distributed decisions. This helps to avoid having a single point of failure in hardware, though the controller as a logical unit could still fail (e.g. bug in the code).
blocks.zh_html: 注意：我们把集中式控制器画成了一个单一实体，但它并不需要运行在单台服务器上。控制平面(control plane)的计算可以跨多台服务器进行，这些服务器协调起来以逻辑集中的方式运作。这与原始模型不同，在原始模型中路由器相互协调但仍然做出自己的分布式决策。这有助于避免硬件层面的单点故障，但控制器作为逻辑单元仍可能失败(例如代码中的 bug)。

blocks.en: Centralization also introduces scalability problems. The controller has to make decisions for everybody, which can get expensive for large networks. By contrast, in a traditional network, each router only has to perform computations for itself.
blocks.zh_html: 集中化(centralization)也引入了可扩展性问题(scalability problems)。控制器必须为所有人做出决策，这对于大型网络来说可能会变得昂贵。相反，在传统网络中，每台路由器只需要为自己执行计算。

blocks.en: Centralization could also introduce different types of complexity. In a traditional network, we could buy a router and connect it, and it more or less starts working right away. With a central controller, we have additional infrastructure challenges. Where do we put this controller? How do we connect it to the individual routers in a reliable way?
blocks.zh_html: 集中化(centralization)还可能引入不同类型的复杂性。在传统网络中，我们可以买一台路由器并连接它，它或多或少可以直接开始工作。有了中央控制器，我们面临额外的基础设施挑战。我们把控制器放在哪里？如何以可靠的方式将它连接到各个路由器？

blocks.en: This is an active area of research, including a project by Sylvia Ratnasamy and Rob Shakir (Berkeley CS 168 instructors).
blocks.zh_html: 这是一个活跃的研究领域，包括 Sylvia Ratnasamy 和 Rob Shakir(Berkeley CS 168 讲师)的一个项目。

blocks.en: SDN in the Management and Data Plane
blocks.zh_html: 管理平面(management plane)和数据平面(data plane)中的 SDN

blocks.en: We’ve seen SDN as a new way to implement the control plane. But, the initial frustration that led to the development of SDN was at the management plane.
blocks.zh_html: 我们已经看到 SDN 是实现控制平面(control plane)的一种新方式。但最初导致 SDN 发展的挫折来自管理平面(management plane)。

blocks.en: It turns out, many of the design paradigms that SDN used at the control plane can also apply to the management plane. For example, we saw that SDN relies on well-defined, programmatic APIs (e.g. OpenFlow).
blocks.zh_html: 事实证明，SDN 在控制平面上使用的许多设计范式也可以应用于管理平面(management plane)。例如，我们看到 SDN 依赖于定义良好的编程 API(如 OpenFlow)。
